method: A self-assessed rubric, not a measurement. Each subsystem has a weight (weights sum to 100). 'implemented' is the share of that subsystem's work that exists in any form, including approximations. 'verified' is the share whose behaviour has been confirmed identical to the original (bit for bit against its machine code, or exact by the loader/table layout in its code). The overall numbers are the weighted sums. The weights and shares are judgement calls and will change as work and understanding grow. The 2026-10-13 review raises the flight-model estimate from 76%/67% to 80%/71% for the recovered delta branch, full-element force composition, wing predicates, bounds writers and ordered grouping. These four-point changes are conservative judgement calls, not percentages derived from test counts. Kernel comparisons with controlled inputs, recorded CRT results or tolerances do not establish whole-simulator equivalence. The subsequent loader-fixture review keeps estimates unchanged: completed original-loader runs replace partial snapshots, but the current ACF object comparison is diagnostic, does not assert parity, and skips when reference aircraft are absent.

subsystems.name: Aircraft files (ACF)
subsystems.note: All properties are preserved; typed: mass, CG, wings, gear, engine and controls subset. Loader schema of 1117 properties extracted; six values confirmed in code. Three original-loader replays now reach the return sentinel (13690, 13718 and 15525 tracked words). Previous fixtures were partial; two contain 424 corrected words each. These are reference results, not a count of matching ported fields. The current object test only reports differences and skips without local reference files.

subsystems.name: 3D models (OBJ8)
subsystems.note: Geometry, nested transforms, rotation/translation animation, textures. No normal/lit maps, instruments, panels or most dynamic animation.

subsystems.name: Airfoil evaluation (AFL)
subsystems.note: All 34 airfoils; the whole profile function (selection, stall, buffet, blending, Mach factor) matches the original bit for bit on 1800 emulator cases.

subsystems.name: Flight model
subsystems.note: An approximate rigid-body model that takes off and flies. Verified against the original machine code in an emulator: the airfoil and per-element aerodynamics, the whole engine update and the propeller force function, the engine controls for every engine kind, the airflow wash, the terrain mesh probes (vertical ray and segment with moving cells), the strut, tire, wheel and body blend contact models, the weight and balance, the input binding query, and the whole flight step block by block: the wing, body and part loops, the landing gear (targets, steering, brakes, drag, strut contact), the wing and body ground contact chain, the hook, tow, float and wave forces, the plug-in force sink, the equations of motion and the integration, the position setter, the attitude, the geographic state, the 4 x 4 matrices and the Euler angles, the flight angles and the end of the step. Remaining recovery and integration work includes scenery-backed terrain and geoid queries, shared-pointer object lookups, per-strip airflow (`0x14121a9b0`), radiator update and runtime caller state; many ported blocks are not yet connected into a running model. The viewer still flies an approximate model, but now runs the recovered positive-delta coefficient branch and ordered wing grouping with recovered aspect/centroid parameters. Since the previous review, controlled original-code comparisons cover delta parameter curves, noise, target coefficients, full-element and force composition, aircraft bounds point emission, wing enable/join predicates and the 49-pass group scan. Full-element delta output matches 2099/2100 words exactly on macOS, with one platform-trigonometry difference checked by tolerance; some corpora use recorded CRT results or synthetic noise. Live wing boundaries, reference state, noise initialization and much of the remaining flight model are approximate. No whole-model parity is established.

subsystems.name: Datarefs and commands
subsystems.note: Registries and catalogs of 5503 datarefs and 3012 commands from the original, its default keyboard map (71 keys), values for 6 datarefs; 30 key commands act in the flight viewer; 2388 datarefs mapped to the field of the flight object or the simulation object that their getter reads (decoded from the getter code).

subsystems.name: Scenery and world
subsystems.note: Airport ground from apt.dat (runways, taxiways, aprons). No DSF, terrain, objects, lights or weather.

subsystems.name: Rendering
subsystems.note: wgpu viewer with lighting and glass. No PBR, shadows, sky, clouds or instrument screens.

subsystems.name: Platforms and distribution
subsystems.note: CI on Linux, macOS and Windows, nightly builds, standard folder layout. No launcher or settings UI.

maintenance.goal: After substantial confirmed progress, review compatibility percentages against evidence, update this file and the roadmap, regenerate README.md and docs/COMPATIBILITY.md with python3 tools/compat_score.py --write, and push the site update. Always state verification limitations.
maintenance.percentage_policy: Keep estimates unchanged when new evidence improves verification quality without establishing broader behaviour coverage.
maintenance.publication: A push to main changing docs or README triggers the Pages workflow; check deployment outcome before claiming the live site is updated.
